correctness.rationale: The one-site anomaly alters exactly one cavity message. Subtree independence gives the ordinary-vacancy ODE and defect-dependent first message; differences at successive vertices solve a signed Volterra recurrence after the transformation \(u=-\log h\). The target change-of-variables Jacobian is \(e^{-u}\). Strict sign follows by clock coupling, the factorial bound by bounded Volterra integrals, and the sharp coefficient by the first-order expansion of the defect message. Fifteen finite-depth numerical checks and exact degree-three, rate-two integrals agree, but do not replace the infinite-volume proof.

originality.rationale: The accessible closest Bethe-lattice primary paper (Penrose & Sudbury 2005, Theorems 12-13) proves homogeneous occupancy and pair correlations, not one-site heterogeneous finite-strength response. Evans (1984) treats translation-invariant filling; Krivelevich et al. (2024) recover homogeneous regular-tree means. A closest indexed one-dimensional anomalous dimer result treats another adsorption object and does not imply this degree-dependent tree law. No stronger directly covering source was found in the checked material; historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Exact finite-amplitude shell response to a single kinetic defect is a natural fundamental invariant for nonequilibrium adsorption on branching substrates. The all-shell sign, sharp factorial attenuation length \(\log(q-1)/(q-2)\), and nonzero coefficient proportional to a-1 give a structural, physically interpretable result not conveyed by homogeneous Bethe-lattice density or pair correlations; no speculative downstream theorem is needed.
